data.title: How small-cap funds shed liquidity risk despite rich valuations
data.description:
A bl.portfolio analysis of liquidity stress data released by the mutual fund industry body AMFI shows that actively managed small-cap mutual funds have reduced their estimated liquidity risk over the past year, despite a sharp rise in valuations.

The Nifty Smallcap 250’s price-to-earnings (PE) ratio rose to 34.45 as of September 30, 2026, from 29.96 a year earlier, indicating richer valuations. However, the category’s average time to liquidate 50 per cent of a portfolio fell to 11.9 days from 17.6 days.

Our analysis suggests that the improvement was driven largely by higher market trading volumes and changes in portfolio composition, including greater exposure to relatively liquid stocks and an increase in the number of holdings.

We analysed AMFI’s liquidity stress-test data for 31 smallcap schemes for September 2025 and September 2026, covering liquidation time for 25 per cent and 50 per cent of portfolios, market-cap allocation, cash holdings, AUM and instrument-wise portfolio composition. Here are the key findings:

Liquidity stress eases

The category’s average time required to liquidate 50 per cent of a portfolio fell to 11.9 days in September 2026 from 17.6 days a year earlier. The time required to liquidate 25 per cent also declined to 6.2 days from nine days.

Of the 31 schemes analysed, 19 recorded an improvement in their 50 per cent liquidation time. Most large schemes saw meaningful improvement. Tata Small Cap reduced its liquidation time from 63 days to 35 days, Quant Small Cap from 71 to 46 days, HDFC Small Cap from 69 to 52 days, SBI Small Cap from 61 to 51 days and Nippon India Small Cap from 43 to 27 days.

Only five schemes saw their liquidation time increase, including Bandhan Small Cap, from 14 to 19 days, and Invesco India Smallcap, from eight to 13 days. Seven schemes reported no change, all of them relatively small schemes.

The improvement was broad-based, particularly among larger schemes, indicating a reduction in estimated liquidity stress even as valuations rose.

Improved trading volumes

One key reason for the improvement was increased trading activity in smallcap stocks. The total traded value of Nifty Smallcap 250 stocks on the NSE rose 24 per cent to ₹31.8 lakh crore during April-September 2026, from ₹25.6 lakh crore during the preceding six months.

This matters because the liquidity stress test estimates the time required to liquidate a portfolio partly on the basis of stocks’ trading volumes. Higher traded volumes mean a given position can theoretically be sold faster, lowering the estimated liquidation time.

Shift towards larger stocks

The share of Nifty 100 stocks in the overall smallcap fund portfolio increased to 22 per cent in September 2026 from 18 per cent a year earlier. These stocks generally have higher trading activity and deeper market liquidity than smaller, less-traded stocks, potentially improving portfolio liquidity.

Seven of the 31 schemes also increased their allocation to midcap stocks. Among them, Quant Small Cap, DSP Small Cap, HDFC Small Cap and Bandhan Small Cap raised their midcap allocation by one to seven percentage points.

However, the trend was not uniform. Axis Small Cap, SBI Small Cap and Nippon India Small Cap increased their smallcap allocation by three to eight percentage points while reducing midcap exposure.

Changes in top-10 holdings

Eighteen of the 31 schemes increased their allocation to their top 10 holdings, while 13 reduced it. The trend was mixed across fund sizes. A higher allocation to the top holdings can support liquidity if these stocks are relatively large and actively traded, enabling fund managers to unwind positions more easily.

More stocks in portfolios

Twenty-two of the 31 schemes increased the number of equity stocks in their portfolios. Bandhan Small Cap added 39 stocks, taking its total to 269 as of September 2026, the highest in the category. JM Small Cap added 27 stocks to reach 88, while Nippon India Small Cap added 21 to reach 256.

A larger number of holdings can reduce dependence on individual stocks and allow funds to spread their positions across more securities. This can reduce the size of individual positions relative to trading volumes and, in turn, lower estimated liquidation times.

What it means for investors

The improvement in liquidity stress is a positive development for smallcap fund investors, particularly as valuations have risen. Higher trading volumes, greater exposure to relatively liquid stocks and broader portfolios have helped reduce the estimated time required to unwind positions.

However, lower stress-test estimates do not guarantee that a fund can exit its holdings quickly during a market-wide sell-off. Liquidity can deteriorate sharply when markets turn volatile and trading volumes dry up.

Investors should therefore view liquidity stress tests as an additional risk indicator, alongside valuations, portfolio concentration, fund size and investment strategy. The bl.portfolio MF Star Ratings can serve as another reference when evaluating funds, but should not be the sole basis for investment decisions.

data.title: Yes Bank reports robust 65% jump in net profit at ₹1,080 cr
data.description:
Yes Bank reported a robust 65 per cent year-on-year jump in second quarter (Q2FY27) standalone net profit at ₹1,080 crore against ₹654 crore in the year ago period on the back of a healthy growth in net interest income and other income and decline in provisions.

In the interest of transparency in view of the recent Supreme Court decision upholding the Bombay High Court judgment and dismissing the appeal filed by the Bank relating to write down of Additional Tier 1 (AT1) Bonds aggregating  ₹8,415 crore, the Bank disclosed that assuming the estimated financial impact of the judgment had been recognised as at September 30, 2026, it would have incurred a loss of ₹5,217 crore in Q2FY27.

Further, the capital adequacy ratio - Basel III would remain unchanged, the annualised return on assets (average) would be negative at 4.3 per cent (proforma) against 0.9 per cent (not recognising the impact of the judgment) in Q2FY27.

Also, the net worth would decline to ₹46,970 crore (₹53,268 crore) and borrowings would increase to the tune of the re-instated bonds ( ₹8,415 crore) to ₹86.149 crore.

Vinay M. Tonse, Managing Director & CEO, Yes Bank,said, “Our Bank delivered another quarter of steady performance, with Net Profit growing 65 per cent year-on-year to  ₹1,080 crore, supported by healthy growth in core operating income and continued improvement in asset quality.”

“We respect the judgment of the Supreme Court relating to the Bank’s Additional Tier 1 Bonds. We are examining it in detail and will take appropriate steps in accordance with the applicable legal and regulatory requirements. We will keep our stakeholders informed as matters progress.”

The Bank said it is presently evaluating the consequential implications of the judgment, including the decisions and actions required to give effect to it, the manner and timing of implementation, and the resulting financial and accounting implications.

Yes Bank is also evaluating, in consultation with its legal advisers, all legal remedies available to it, including such further proceedings as may be maintainable before the Supreme Court.

“Pending completion of this evaluation and determination of the consequential actions and appropriate accounting treatment, the potential financial impact arising from the judgment has not been recognised in the books of account or incorporated in the reported financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026,” the Bank said.

data.title: Should you subscribe to Zetwerk’s IPO?
data.description:
The IPO of Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses is open for subscription until Monday. The company, which runs a tech-based manufacturing platform, expects to raise ₹2,830 crore, while promoters and existing investors, including Peak XV, Accel and Lightspeed, are offering shares worth ₹2,182 crore through an offer-for-sale (OFS).

The promoter and promoter group stake, currently about 21 per cent, is expected to fall to 16 per cent after the IPO, before considering the dilution from ESOP shares. The company intends to pay down debt of ₹2,160 crore (out of ₹3,366 crore as of August 31, 2026) and use the remaining proceeds for acquisitions and general corporate purposes.

At the upper end of the IPO price band, Zetwerk is valued at an enterprise value of around ₹24,225 crore or at about 58x FY26 adjusted EBITDA. The eight-year-old start-up has no listed peers and is yet to become profitable.

Zetwerk operates at the intersection of two key areas of investor interest today — technology and manufacturing. It serves customers in sectors such as energy, consumer electronics, aerospace and precision engineering. However, considering the company’s profitability and the factors mentioned under ‘What doesn’t work’, the asking multiple looks expensive in our view. We recommend that investors give the IPO a pass for now and consider investing after listing, once they have greater conviction in the company’s execution capabilities.

What it does

Zetwerk serves companies operating in sectors such as utilities, renewables, consumer electronics, aerospace, defence, oil & gas and AI (the ‘customers’). Its customers include marquee names such as Siemens Gamesa, Acer, boAt, CG Power, NTPC, Indian Oil, DRDO and the Indian Air Force. When a customer is in need of intermediate components/ inputs in the manufacturing process or is looking to outsource the manufacturing of certain components, it sends the order to Zetwerk.

At the other end, Zetwerk is connected to about 7,000 manufacturers (called third party suppliers), often MSMEs with low capacity utilisation and looking for scale. These third-party suppliers are capable of processes such as stamping, fabrication, machining, forging, die casting and assembling, and are spread across several countries including the US, Taiwan, Vietnam, Germany, Spain and Mexico, besides India.

Zetwerk now chooses an appropriate supplier(s) and sends the order to them for execution. Once the supplier is ready to deliver, Zetwerk purchases the goods from the supplier(s) and sells them to its customer. Contracts with customers are on principal-to-principal basis and Zetwerk is eventually accountable to deliver quality products as per the customer’s specifications. To ensure this, it deploys more than 2,250 operations staff at supplier facilities to coordinate production and supervise quality.

To complement the capacities of the suppliers in the network, Zetwerk has also built its own manufacturing facilities (both greenfield and acquired) for some processes such as assembling and finishing. Here, Zetwerk procures materials, employs labour and manages the process risk.

All these operations are managed through Zetwerk’s proprietary platform, Zetwerk OS, which covers the entire process — from order enquiries and supplier selection to quality assurance and logistics. Customers also get real-time visibility into order status.

These activities form Zetwerk’s first operating segment, ‘Manufacturing business’. The segment generated revenue of ₹9,375 crore in FY26, of which about a third came from its own manufacturing facilities (see chart for growth and margins). Products delivered include wind turbines, transformers, transmission switchgears, wires, cables, railway girders, washing machine motherboards, headsets, wearables and space antennae.

Zetwerk’s suppliers regularly use ferrous and non-ferrous metals and materials such as petrochemicals. The company negotiates bulk or repeat orders with large mills and manufacturers to secure lower prices. Leveraging this purchasing advantage, it has built a separate trading platform for these materials, selling them at a small markup (see chart for margin). Buyers include not only suppliers in Zetwerk’s network but also other businesses. Small-scale operators that may not otherwise benefit from bulk purchasing can also use the platform. This constitutes Zetwerk’s second operating segment, ‘Ecosystem business’.

Key business stats

Between FY24 and FY26, overall revenue has grown at a CAGR of 13.5 per cent, EBITDA at 293 per cent and adjusted EBITDA (adjusted for ESOP cost) at 108 per cent. Revenue from the core manufacturing segment has grown at a higher CAGR of 24 per cent.

Within manufacturing, energy products (solar modules, transformers, switchgears, wires, wind turbine nacelle sub-assembly, etc.), precision products (wearables, laptops, displays, PCBs, EV chargers, machined/ cast/ fabricated metal products, etc.) and capital goods (process equipment like reactors, tanks, steel structures, etc.) accounted for 69, 15 and 16 per cent of FY26 manufacturing revenue. These sub-segments have grown at CAGRs of 25, 55 and 5.5 per cent, over the same period.

Geographically, India, the US and the rest of the world have accounted for about 80, 18 and 2 per cent of FY24-26 overall revenue on average.

What works

Manufacturing revenue from repeat customers has improved from 78 per cent in FY24 to 80 per cent in FY26 and to 89 per cent in Q1 FY27. Net revenue retention rate stands at a median of 1.29x over FY24-26. This indicates that repeat customers have roughly given Zetwerk 29 per cent more business in the current year than the preceding year. These metrics show Zetwerk’s ability to consistently deliver on quality, especially given it works with the above marquee names.

New manufacturing order inflows were ₹15,393 in FY26, having grown at a CAGR of 31 per cent. Currently, the manufacturing order book stands at ₹13,062 crore or 1.4x FY26 manufacturing revenue.

Zetwerk gets both ‘built-to-print’ and ‘original design manufacturing (ODM)’ orders. ODM orders require Zetwerk to design the product on its own besides manufacturing it, while built-to-print orders do not. ODM orders typically have higher realisation. Share of ODM revenue has risen from 8 per cent in FY24 to 14 per cent in FY26.

Above all, the share of revenue from own manufacturing facilities is also on the rise — from 7 per cent in FY24 to 33 per cent in FY26. As captive manufacturing is a relatively recent initiative, rising scale of operations could create scope for margin expansion. Here’s how. When Zetwerk executes an order purely at the facilities of third-party suppliers, it purchase cost also includes the supplier’s margin. Producing the order at its own facilities, even partially, allows Zetwerk to retain some or all of that margin. The customer’s quoted price (Zetwerk’s selling price) remains the same in either case.

What doesn’t work

One, some of the company’s past decisions could raise concerns about its ability to execute and allocate capital effectively. Towards the end of FY26, it discontinued its third segment ‘Civil infrastructure works’, which involved building water pipelines and railway tracks, after the segment proved to be a drag on working capital.

The segment’s assets and liabilities are now classified as held for sale and are expected to be disposed by end of FY27. The segment’s net losses (attributable to equity owners) in FY24-FY26 were ₹65 crore, ₹156 crore and ₹642 crore, respectively, compared with losses of ₹854 crore, ₹210 crore and ₹991 crore, respectively, from the other two segments (continuing operations). However, the latter figure for FY26 was only about ₹195 crore after adjusting for a net-worth-neutral one-off item. For perspective, adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations stood at ₹97 crore, ₹323 crore and ₹421 crore over FY24-FY26.

Net exceptional losses from continuing operations in FY24-FY26 were ₹372 crore, ₹84 crore and ₹39 crore, respectively, after adjusting for the net-worth-neutral one-off item, taking the cumulative loss to ₹495 crore. Of the ₹616 crore in exceptional items, provisions for bad debts, supplier advances and unbilled revenue, impairment allowances and restructuring expenses accounted for a significant portion.

Management explained that most of these expenses related to the discontinued segment. Losses of this magnitude could have been avoided had management recognised the business’s working-capital-intensive nature before entering it. The prospectus also mentions an apparel trading business discontinued in FY24. An impairment loss of ₹62 crore against this investment is included in the ₹616 crore of exceptional items cited above.

Two, positive operating cash flows turned negative after accounting for working capital changes, in each of the three years. The trend continued into Q1 FY27.

Three, the business model allows room for leakages — meaning, some customers may try to bypass Zetwerk and send orders directly to the third-party suppliers. However, management’s defence is that the company can offer customers quotations competitive with market prices.

Four, the energy products sub-segment, which accounts for 69 per cent of manufacturing revenue, has gained significant momentum, with a revenue CAGR of 25 per cent, partly driven by the boom in AI-related capital expenditure. This growth could slow if sentiment around AI turns negative.

Five, auditors made several adverse observations in FY24 and FY25, including weaknesses in the internal audit system and the absence of a robust mechanism for physical inventory verification. They also cited ineffective internal controls over certain processes, potentially exposing revenue and receivables to misstatement risks. The absence of adverse remarks in FY26 and Q1 FY27 suggests that the company may have taken corrective action.

Overall, the company appears to have tried to clean up its books and present a couple of stable businesses to public shareholders, ahead of its IPO — which is a plus. However, the asking price appears particularly steep against this backdrop and a volatile equity market. Prudent, value-conscious investors may want a margin of safety against execution slip-ups, before considering the offer.

data.title: Trump's Russian oil tariff waiver offers India relief, but experts warn of renewed US pressure
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- US President Donald Trump's decision to waive additional tariffs of 100 per cent on major buyers of Russian oil has provided immediate relief to India, reducing the risk of fresh trade penalties and offering Indian refiners greater flexibility in crude purchases. However, experts warned that the benefits remain uncertain and will depend on global oil prices, supply conditions and future US trade policy.

Trump signed an Executive Order on Friday implementing the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, while simultaneously waiving several sanctions and additional duties under the legislation.

The order provides for additional tariffs of 100 per cent on goods from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil and natural gas making fresh purchases from October 18, but suspends their application through a presidential waiver.

"Pursuant to section 115(a) of the Graham Act, I hereby waive the application of any duties provided for in sections 112 and 113 of the Graham Act or this order," the White House Executive Order stated.

The waiver has no fixed expiry date and can be withdrawn, while existing Russia-related sanctions under other Executive Orders remain unaffected.

According to the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), the decision provides India temporary relief but leaves open the possibility of Washington restoring tariff pressure during future trade negotiations.

In its report titled "U.S. Waives Russian-Oil Tariffs: Temporary Relief for India, but Uncertainty Remains," GTRI said, "For India, the waiver buys time but offers no lasting certainty."

R Ramachandran, former Director (Refineries) at Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), told ANI that the immediate benefit for Indian oil companies would be greater crude sourcing flexibility rather than necessarily higher refining margins.

"So more than the GRM, what actually impact it will have on Indian refineries will be the availability of more crude choices," he said.

Gross refining margin (GRM) refers to the difference between the value of petroleum products produced by a refinery and the cost of crude oil processed.

Ramachandran explained that increased Russian crude availability could help refiners secure more economical supplies, depending on discounts. However, lower crude prices could also be accompanied by falling petroleum product prices, limiting gains in refining margins.

Rajani Sinha, Chief Economist at CareEdge, said Russia's importance to India has increasingly shifted from discounted oil towards ensuring uninterrupted supplies.

"The discount has really reduced significantly. But yes, what is more important for India now is availability and ensuring consistent supply of crude oil for the economy," Sinha told ANI.

She said Russia's share of India's crude imports had exceeded 30 per cent in recent years, although its price advantage over international benchmarks had narrowed.

GTRI noted that Russia's share in India's oil imports declined from 51 per cent in July to 44 per cent in August as purchases shifted towards the United States and the United Arab Emirates.

The think tank also highlighted Washington's own energy requirements as a possible factor behind the waiver.

According to its report, the United States agreed to purchase Russian diesel under an October 9 agreement to address domestic fuel shortages and elevated prices.

It also noted that Washington had agreed not to raise tariffs on China until January 10, suggesting that targeting India alone could complicate ongoing bilateral trade negotiations.

"The message is clear: U.S. interests determine when penalties apply, while the ability to retaliate helps secure protection," GTRI founder Ajay Srivastava said in the report.

Meanwhile, Ramachandran said a sustained waiver could help reduce freight costs and ease logistical constraints associated with Russian oil shipments.

He said greater vessel availability and smoother payment arrangements could improve crude procurement economics.

"If Russia and India can agree upon on a continued ruble-rupee exchange for this, it also supports to ease the foreign exchange outgo which currently is affecting the Indian Rupee's strength," he said.

However, these benefits would depend on the restrictions that remain applicable.

On the broader economic impact, Sinha said India's current account deficit could remain manageable despite elevated crude prices, supported by merchandise and services exports.

She expects the current account deficit to remain between 0.8 and 1.2 per cent of GDP, assuming crude prices range between USD 80 and USD 100 per barrel during the remaining financial year.

However, persistently higher prices could widen the deficit towards 1.5 per cent of GDP under adverse conditions.

Sinha expects average inflation of around 5 to 5.5 per cent, although higher fuel costs and food inflation remain risks.

She said the fiscal impact would depend on whether elevated oil costs are absorbed through excise duty reductions, oil marketing companies or higher retail fuel prices.

Healthy tax collections and potential disinvestment receipts, including from IDBI Bank, could help the government manage fiscal pressures, she added.

On the rupee, Sinha said the waiver could improve market sentiment but was unlikely to provide substantial direct support to the currency.

She also stressed that a lasting India-US trade agreement would offer greater economic stability than temporary tariff relief, warning that fresh US tariff threats could emerge.

Ramachandran cautioned against immediately entering long-term Russian crude supply agreements without clarity on the waiver's duration.

"The first thing I would say is that it is too early to look at jumping into long-term contracts," he said.

He added that refiners would need to assess whether Russian crude discounts and stable supply conditions could be sustained.

GTRI similarly warned India against making permanent trade concessions in exchange for temporary relief.

"India should protect its energy security, buy oil on commercial terms and prepare for renewed U.S. pressure. Temporary tariff relief is no basis for permanent trade concessions," Srivastava said.

data.title: Arbitrum Courts European Investors Managing €800 Billion With New Revenue Pitch
data.description:
TL;DR: Arbitrum representatives have presented the network’s infrastructure and revenue model to European financial institutions managing substantial assets. The meetings should not be confused with confirmed investment commitments to ARB.

Arbitrum is increasingly pitching itself as a blockchain infrastructure business rather than simply another cryptocurrency ecosystem.

During institutional meetings reported on October 16, representatives discussed the network’s commercial potential with European banks, wealth managers and other professional investors. The participating organisations were said to represent more than €800 billion in assets under management.

That figure describes the institutions attending the presentations. It does not represent money invested in Arbitrum or its native token.

Explaining The Business Behind The Blockchain

The discussions placed particular emphasis on how blockchain infrastructure can earn fees through licensing, network services and support for financial applications.

Research presented alongside WisdomTree material explored Arbitrum’s financial performance and the possibility of building sustainable revenue rather than relying on speculative token trading.

Institutional projects using Arbitrum technology are one possible route toward such a model. They demonstrate how a financial business might adopt blockchain infrastructure without requiring its customers to trade ARB directly.

Arbitrum’s community has also discussed new ways to generate revenue for its DAO treasury.

Interest Is Not Adoption

The meetings do not confirm that any participating bank has committed to deploy the technology, purchase tokens or establish a product.

For Arbitrum, the next task is converting conversations into actual commercial integrations. Banks will demand clear answers about reliability, compliance, privacy and the economics of using blockchain rails.

Still, the change in emphasis is notable. Blockchain companies increasingly want to be assessed on the value of the services they provide, not simply the price of their coins.

data.title: Nine crypto firms form Quantum Alliance to set post-quantum standards
data.description:
Nine crypto organizations have teamed up to answer a question the industry has mostly been answering with marketing copy: what does "quantum-resistant" actually mean?

The group, called the Quantum Alliance, launched on October 15-16, 2026. Its stated mission is to define and test quantum-resistant standards for blockchain networks, and to make anyone claiming quantum resistance prove it against verifiable criteria.

The founding members include leaders from Quantus, American Fortress and Intmax, alongside other blockchain organizations that round out the group of nine.

The alliance says it will produce open definitions and standards for post-quantum readiness. The focus areas include transaction signatures and key management, the two places where a quantum attack would hurt most.

The work is split across four initial working groups:

Blockchain migration. How existing networks move from today's cryptography to quantum-resistant alternatives without breaking everything along the way.

Post-quantum zero-knowledge proof systems. Zero-knowledge proofs let someone prove a statement is true without revealing the underlying data. The group will look at versions of these systems built to survive quantum attacks.

Wallet and key security. Where user funds actually live, and where most of the practical risk sits.

Cross-chain compatibility. Making sure one chain's quantum fix does not leave it unable to talk to everyone else's.

The alliance has committed to publishing all of its outputs publicly.

Most existing blockchain networks rely on elliptic-curve signatures to prove who owns what. The concern is Shor's algorithm. Running on a sufficiently powerful future quantum computer, it could potentially work backward from a public key to the private key that controls the funds.

Blockchains are permanent records, and the public keys sitting on them are not going anywhere. An estimated 6.04 million to 6.4 million BTC, approximately 30.2% of the total supply, have public keys exposed at rest. Those coins sit at addresses where the public key is already visible on-chain, which is exactly the input a quantum attacker would need.

The broader cryptography world has already done some of the groundwork. NIST finalized its post-quantum cryptography standards in August 2024, giving governments and enterprises a set of approved algorithms to start migrating toward.

Blockchains, though, have problems that NIST's work does not neatly solve. Signatures get bigger with post-quantum schemes, which affects block space and fees. Migration requires coordination across thousands of independent users and node operators. And funds held by people who never move them cannot be upgraded on anyone's schedule but their own.

That is the gap the Quantum Alliance is targeting: taking general-purpose post-quantum standards and translating them into criteria that fit how blockchains actually work. The migration framework is aimed squarely at protecting vulnerable public keys like the ones holding those exposed Bitcoin balances.

For builders, open standards could lower the cost of doing this properly. A wallet developer or a bridge team would no longer have to design post-quantum security from scratch or guess what other chains will adopt. The cross-chain working group is especially relevant here, since a fragmented approach could leave assets safe on one network and exposed the moment they move to another.

For holders, coins sitting at addresses with exposed public keys carry a different long-term risk profile than coins that have never revealed their keys.

The founding roster also matters. The names publicly attached so far, Quantus, American Fortress and Intmax, are not the largest players in the industry. Whether the alliance becomes a reference point or remains a niche working group will likely depend on whether bigger networks, wallet providers and custodians decide to adopt or at least engage with its outputs.

data.title: ICICI Bank sees another margin squeeze in Q3 as FCNR-B costs kick in
data.description:
Mumbai, Oct. 17 -- ICICI Bank Ltd, India's second largest private-sector bank, expects its net interest margin (NIM) to dip marginally in the December quarter as the full cost of foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) deposits raised in the September quarter kicks in, before margins begin to recover.

"The full impact would largely get reflected in the third quarter, after which we expect the margins to start moving up, even based on the current level of policy rates," executive director Sandeep Batra said at a post-earnings press conference on Saturday.

The private lender's net interest margin (NIM)-the difference between a bank's earnings on loans and investments and its cost of deposits and borrowings-fell to 4.18% in the September quarter from 4.36% in the June quarter.

Its net interest income still grew 17.7% year-on-year to Rs.25,339 crore, and profit before tax rose 20.4% to Rs.19,724 crore. Excluding treasury, which posted a Rs.230 crore loss as government bond yields rose, profit before tax grew 23.4% to Rs.19,954 crore.

Batra attributed about 9-10 basis points (bps) of the margin decline to a change in the bank's deposit mix after it mobilized about $18 billion in FCNR-B deposits under the Reserve Bank of India's swap facility. Of this, about $10 billion was leveraged by the bank itself, about $3.6 billion came through partner banks, and about $4.6 billion came from retail depositors who took no leverage. One basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point.

The inflows lifted total deposits 27.1% on-year, compared with 17% excluding FCNR-B, and pulled the average current and savings account ratio down to 35.8% from 38.1% in the June quarter.

Batra said the bank had done better than it initially expected under a scheme he described as meeting "an overall national need for foreign exchange".

The landed cost of these deposits, which is the all-in cost to the bank after paying interest to non-resident depositors and covering the expense of hedging the dollar funds against rupee swings, came to about 6.5%. That is slightly higher than the 6.30-6.40% the bank had estimated in their July post-earnings call, when the scheme was just launched.

The deposits run for three to five years and are exempt from reserve and priority-sector lending requirements, allowing the bank to lend the full amount. Part of the money has gone into repaying bulk deposits and funding loans, and the rest will be deployed over the next two quarters.

Total loans grew 30% on-year, or 24.1% excluding loans made by overseas branches against FCNR-B deposits. Domestic corporate loans rose 30.6%, which the management linked to capital expenditure, longer working capital cycles, a shift by companies from bond markets to bank borrowing and firms building liquidity buffers. The credit card book, however, shrank 9.7% on-year. They attributed this mainly to a high base, as festive spending began early last year, along with the bank's exit from customer segments it found unprofitable. "It is not a credit issue," Batra said.

The management said the bank's view is that RBI could raise the repo rate twice more by 25bps each, taking it to about 6%, while the central bank gradually withdraws surplus liquidity from the banking system. Since a large share of ICICI Bank's loans is linked to the repo rate, loan rates adjust faster than deposit rates in a hiking cycle, a pattern they expect to repeat this time.

The bank said the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India's (Irdai) consultation paper on distribution economics would have little effect on its earnings. The paper proposes capping commissions on single-premium life cover packaged with loans at 2% and describes such cover as "near mandatory in practice". That provision directly affects banks and non-banks that sell insurance alongside loans.

Batra said bancassurance fees account for less than 1% of the bank's total income and about 5% of its fee income, and that it sells insurance only from ICICI group companies. Asked whether its ties with group insurers would change if the paper is adopted as proposed, he said "nothing will change", adding that the impact on the bank's profit would be "absolutely minimal".

data.title: Nearly All Volume on FIFA-Linked Prediction Market Is Circular Trading — WSJ
data.description:
By Caitlin Ostroff and Katherine Long

ADI Predictstreet, a newcomer to prediction markets, made a high-profile debut during World Cup broadcasts after paying FIFA more than $150 million to become the global soccer organization's official partner.

Since late August, nearly every transaction on the platform has been made by a small network of linked accounts, according to an analysis of public data, suggesting that most of its trading volume is inauthentic.

About $108 million of the total $167 million in transactions that have been made on ADI Predictstreet through late September were made by cryptocurrency wallets that appear to be linked to the company, the data shows.

The accounts have almost exclusively traded with one another and are funded by a single cryptocurrency wallet that also collects the platform's trading fees, the data shows. Typically, trading fees are collected by wallets associated with a platform's owner.

ADI Predictstreet launched in April as part of a conglomerate led by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, a member of Abu Dhabi's royal family known as the "spy sheikh," who serves as Abu Dhabi's deputy ruler and national security adviser for the United Arab Emirates. The company's deal with FIFA gave it exclusive advertising rights during 2026 World Cup matches. ADI Predictstreet aims to be "the world's leading prediction market platform, with millions of active users," according to the FIFA Museum's website.

ADI Predictstreet didn't respond to requests for comment. FIFA declined to comment.

The unusual trading patterns were identified by three Harvard University students — Joshua Gupta, William Thompson and Ashwin Vinod Kumar — who analyzed public blockchain data. The Wall Street Journal shared the students' analysis with experts who study unusual trading activity in cryptocurrency markets. These experts concluded that trading on the platform appeared to be inorganic.

"In this case, it looks like some of the trading fees are getting recycled back into the wallets doing the trading, and the only people who would have access to these funds are the platform themself," said Rajiv Sethi, an economics professor at Barnard College. Crypto-tracking company Solidus Labs also verified the students' analysis.

Unusual trading began on the platform during the World Cup in early July. Two cryptocurrency wallets traded more than $81 million with each other across hundreds of different markets, some days amounting to more than 90% of trading volume on the platform. Both wallets were funded by an account that also collects trading fees for ADI Predictstreet.

After the World Cup, ADI Predictstreet's trading volume dropped significantly. Overall, roughly 26,000 wallets have ever traded on the platform, the data shows. But since late August, a network of 795 wallets — again all funded by the fee-collecting account — have accounted for 99% of the activity on the platform, the analysis showed.

"The retail activity looks almost dead," said Andre Guettler, a finance professor at Germany's Ulm University.

By late September, the most hotly traded market on ADI Predictstreet's platform was whether Democrat Ron Nirenberg, the former mayor of San Antonio, would win his race for Bexar County judge against Republican Patrick Von Dohlen. More than $650,000 appears to have been bet for or against Nirenberg, who the platform shows trading at 94% odds.

Every single trade in that market was made by one of the 795 company-linked wallets, the data shows, which traded among one another for roughly 10 days in September. The market has seen no trading since.

Nirenberg said in an interview that he hadn't previously heard of ADI Predictstreet. In general, prediction markets on elections worry him, he said. "My instinct says it's not helpful to our democracy." Von Dohlen echoed those sentiments, adding that he believes his odds are significantly better than the platform predicts. "It certainly is very problematic to have outside and foreign influence in United States elections," he said.

By comparison, combined trading volume on the much larger prediction markets Polymarket and Kalshi was less than $55,000 on the Bexar County contest as of Friday.

ADI Predictstreet is licensed by the gambling division of Gibraltar, which has embraced the moniker "Blockchain Rock" in trumpeting its openness to the crypto industry. In an interview Wednesday, Andrew Lyman, Gibraltar's gambling commissioner, said a preliminary review of the trading patterns surfaced by the Journal found ADI is in compliance with Gibraltar's regulations, which prohibit "self-trading."

"There has been no consumer detriment," Lyman said.

On Tuesday, after the Journal began asking Gibraltar's gambling division about Predictstreet, the ADI Foundation, Predictstreet's sister nonprofit, signed a memorandum with Gibraltar pledging to work with the territory on promoting cryptocurrencies.

ADI Predictstreet is listed in a June public filing as a subsidiary of the investment firm International Holding Company, whose chairman is Tahnoon. A company backed by Tahnoon also owns 49% of World Liberty Financial, the Trump family's crypto venture, the Journal previously reported.

Shruti Choudhury, a spokeswoman for the investment firm, said it is "IHC's position that ADI Predictstreet is not a subsidiary of IHC." Choudhury didn't respond to additional questions.

Since last year, the ADI Foundation has also signed partnerships with companies including Visa, Mastercard, BlackRock, Franklin Templeton and Bank of New York Mellon to popularize the cryptocurrency blockchain on which the prediction market is based.

In late 2025, Ajay Bhatia, chief executive of ADI's parent company, agreed to pay about $170,000 to settle insider-trading allegations with India's securities regulator, pertaining to information he allegedly shared while CEO of another Tahnoon-backed company. Bhatia didn't respond to requests for comment.

data.title: My Daughter and I Went Into Business Together. It Has Been an Adjustment. — WSJ
data.description:
By Bob Brody | Photography by Alessio Paduano for WSJ

In the 62 years since my first job, I've worked alongside thousands of people. But three years ago, I found myself in an entirely new kind of working relationship. My new partner was my daughter, Caroline Chirichella.

I'm a boomer, 74, and she's a millennial, exactly half my age. Joining a new business has required a lot of adapting, and a lot of patience. Caroline trusts her gut, while I'm more deliberate, analytical and systematic. She often talks faster than I can listen, and listens faster than I can talk, grasping my meaning before I finish a sentence.

There are certain things I feel I'm more qualified to do than she is. At the same time, I'm clueless about how to navigate Instagram and TikTok, let alone master search-engine optimization issues and create websites and webinars.

But perhaps the biggest challenge of working with my daughter is that I not only need to adapt to her style, but also to recognize that she is her own person and I need her to be herself.

A difficult dynamic

Any family collaboration in business, of course, takes a delicate touch. Transitioning from parenting a child to partnering with a full-grown adult can be difficult. Clashes between family members in business can lead to tensions that sever a personal relationship, experts warn.

I never thought I'd be teaming up with my daughter. Then, after successful careers as an opera singer and chef, Caroline decided to branch out into public relations, a field I've been in for 35 years. At first, she asked my advice now and then. But soon she was running a thriving one-woman shop with an expanding clientele. So, I volunteered to join her, part-time and pro bono.

Mainly, I'm on call to be of counsel and give top-line, big-picture guidance. But I also get some dirt under my fingernails with Zoom calls, brainstorms, writing and pitching. All in all, I do only about 20% of the heavy lifting, a division of labor perfectly agreeable to us both.

We get many mutual advantages from going shoulder to shoulder. At the very least, she gets more attention, interest and care from me than she's likely to get at any job.

I, on the other hand, get the opportunity to train her as I once mentored junior staff at global PR agencies. Except now I'm helping to develop my own daughter, a mother of two, into a full-fledged professional and family breadwinner.

My daughter and I have adopted certain basic operating principles that serve us well. I'm long on compliments, but also never skimp on critiques. I never pretend my every word is gospel. We never talk business at the family dinner table.

I encourage Caroline to disagree with me however much she deems necessary. But that is a moot point: Ever since she was a toddler she's never hesitated to take issue with me.

Contrasting styles

Still, we approach our jobs with different styles, and we've had to make plenty of adjustments along the way.

I've practiced my profession exactly seven times longer than Caroline. So, inevitably I'm convinced I can perform pretty much any task better than she, and figure I can best educate Caroline through my example. But Caroline is a do-it-yourself kind of millennial, so I've had to shift gears, and explain how and why a chore should be carried out, and then let Caroline do it.

Likewise, Caroline is by nature quick on the trigger. She thinks fast, decides fast and acts fast. She might immediately express enthusiasm for a concept from a client that still requires further research, for instance. Or need to take time to revise a document to avoid oversights and mistakes. To my mind, she rushes. "Slow down, take your time," I tell her, but so far to little avail.

We also communicate in different ways. I came of age professionally when people still primarily gathered in person or spoke by phone, all in real time, whereas Caroline grew up often staying in touch with people through the internet.

I've suggested we two hold weekly or bimonthly meetings — informal yet complete with agendas to better establish our priorities — to introduce structure, rhythm and ritual to our partnership. Caroline pays lip service — "Yes, good idea!" she'll say — but has never committed to it. No doubt this aversion is in part due to her responsibilities as the mother of young children. But I've also come to understand that millennials prefer to be more freewheeling, less regimented and "corporate," than baby boomers. So instead, we catch up on pending and pressing matters if and when suitable opportunities randomly arise.

No face to face

Similarly, I often recommended Caroline and I get together to talk shop face to face. Our houses are less than half a mile apart. But we seldom do. Caroline prefers to discuss business through email, Facebook Messenger or Zoom.

To me, this online preference — again, understandable with two young children — can lead to problems. Recently, a client of ours complained through email about our services. I advised Caroline that if the client could see our faces and hear our voices, she might better understand and appreciate the value we brought to the table. Instead, Caroline responded through emails.

Ultimately, the client quit over what I interpreted to be misunderstandings on both sides. Caroline sees it differently: The client, in her view, changed her priorities during the project and grew frustrated with new, unrealistic expectations.

Over time, I'm trying to cultivate a lighter touch and be a little more hands-off, and I think it has made our working relationship stronger. The same goes for our father-daughter relationship.

Our collaboration has brought us closer, too, forging newfound respect and trust, along with deepening our appreciation and love for each other. For the life of me, I'm hard-pressed to imagine a greater reward.

Write to reports@wsj.com

data.title: China Mobile Hong Kong Establishes Hong Kong's First U6G Network
data.description:
Expanding Next-Generation Network Capabilities and Accelerating the Innovative Convergence of Communication, Computing, and AI Laying a Solid Foundation for 6G Development in Hong Kong

HONG KONG, Oct. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- China Mobile Hong Kong Company Limited ("China Mobile Hong Kong") announced that it has taken the lead in realising a U6GHz network, successfully completing network testing and validation at its Mong Kok flagship store and advancing the exploration of Upper 6GHz band applications in mobile networks. Implementing China Mobile Group's strategy of "strengthening the network foundation and full-stack innovation", China Mobile Hong Kong aims to enhance network capabilities through new frequency band applications, drive collaborative innovation between terminals and the wider industry, and lay a robust foundation for Hong Kong's future 6G development.

Strategic Early Deployment of New Spectrum to Build Momentum for a 6G FutureU6GHz, or the Upper 6GHz band, can provide continuous wide bandwidth and is a crucial spectrum resource supporting 5G-A and future 6G evolution. On 29 November 2024, Hong Kong completed its 6/7GHz spectrum auction, becoming the first region globally to auction this frequency band for public mobile services. China Mobile Hong Kong successfully bid for 100MHz of continuous spectrum and has made appropriate forward-looking deployments, advancing network capability validation and terminal adaptation to accumulate experience for future 6G commercialisation.

Expanding Network Capacity to Enable Smoother Smart ApplicationsThe newly added U6GHz spectrum can be utilised synergistically with existing frequency bands. Through various combinations with current spectrums, it can achieve download speeds of 3Gbps. The increased availability of spectrum helps enhance data transmission capabilities, accommodating more simultaneous user connections, improving the internet experience in highly congested areas, and supporting high-definition video and large-capacity data transmission.

As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly integrated into production and daily life, the demand for data transmission from devices such as smart glasses and AI robots continues to rise. China Mobile Hong Kong will promote the synergistic development of U6GHz and intelligent computing services, enhance connectivity between terminals and intelligent computing platforms, and explore AI image analysis, immersive interactions, and industrial applications. This will allow smart services to better integrate into everyday life and corporate operations.

Aligning with Mainland China and Hong Kong Blueprints to Consolidate the Foundation of Digital-Intelligent DevelopmentChina Mobile Hong Kong will actively align with the Nation's "15th Five-Year Plan" and Hong Kong's first Five-Year Plan. Focusing on "AI+", computing infrastructure, and new industrialisation, the company will enhance communication and smart services through network upgrades to assist Hong Kong in building an international innovation and technology centre. Concurrently, China Mobile Hong Kong will collaborate with industry partners to accelerate the research, development, and testing of U6GHz products. By expanding hotspot coverage according to demand, it aims to drive the maturity of the industrial ecosystem and accelerate Hong Kong's 6G development. Looking ahead, China Mobile Hong Kong will continue to leverage its strengths as a central state-owned enterprise, providing high-quality digital infrastructure to serve Hong Kong and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, thereby fully contributing to the building of a cyber superpower and a digital China.

About China Mobile Hong Kong LimitedChina Mobile Hong Kong Company Limited ("China Mobile Hong Kong") is the wholly-owned subsidiary of China Mobile Limited (HKEx: 941), which is listed on the Fortune Global 500. China Mobile Hong Kong was incepted in January 1997 and was the first mobile network operator to launch PCS services in Hong Kong.

As the world's leading mobile network brand with the largest customer base*, The Company offers innovative and comprehensive 5G communications services, including voice, data, IDD and international roaming. The Company is committed to the development of 5G with new technologies such as artificial intelligence, internet of things, cloud computing and big data, integrating 5G applications in different industries, promoting the construction and development of smart city groups in Greater Bay Area.

* China Mobile (Hong Kong) Limited is a wholly-owned subsidiary of China Mobile Limited. As of 31 December 2025, China Mobile Limited had the largest number of mobile network subscribers in the world.

data.title: Real estate stocks surge as rate hike odds decrease
data.description:
Real estate stocks surged as odds of a rate hike in the October 27–28 Federal Open Market Committee meeting fell further.

According to the CME FedWatch tool, the probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike decreased to 15.5% from 17.7% a week ago and 55.4% a month ago.

Economists are questioning the effectiveness of rate shifts as a tool to fight inflation within an AI economy, according to a recent report by S&P Global Market Intelligence.

"AI is not sensitive to interest rates because most investors in AI expect returns of 10%, 20%, sometimes 30%," Torsten Slok, chief economist at Apollo Global Management, reportedly said. "From this perspective, it doesn't matter if the Fed hikes 25 bps because the expected return on AI is expected to be so much higher than the level of the fed funds rate."

The rate-insensitive AI boom is leading to an economic phenomenon where rapid growth in one sector tends to lead to declines in other sectors. In this case, AI is likely draining capital and labor from sectors such as housing and automobiles, which will likely be hit harder as rates are hiked further, the economist said.

Besides, one or two more increases this year will do little to curb soaring crude oil prices or increase diesel supply, according to another report by Market Intelligence.

"There is growing concern that the Fed's conventional policy tools are not able to resolve the problems in the Middle East and probably won't do much to deter the tech investment boom given investor appetite to not be left behind," James Knightley, chief international economist at ING, told Market Intelligence in an interview.

"I don't see the Fed losing credibility here," Michael O'Rourke, chief market strategist with JonesTrading, reportedly said. "It is simply a challenging environment that lacks good options."

The S&P 500 Real Estate Index Sector (SP500-60) increased 1.15% week-over-week to 269.1 points, while the accompanying State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF was up 1.32% to $42.16.

The Dow Jones REIT Indx Equity REIT Total Return Index advanced 1.17%, while the FTSE Nareit All Equity REITs index added 1.15%.

Weekly Winners & Losers

CoStar Group led the weekly advancers, adding 8.90% from the prior week to close at $32.31. The week saw RBC Capital Markets say the real estate information services company is poised to beat the Q3 earnings estimate and raise full-year financial guidance.

Host Hotels & Resorts followed with a 5.83% advance week-over-week to $23.97.

Hotel REIT stocks were surging in a week that saw Freedom Broker initiate coverage of five major U.S. hotel stocks with Buy ratings. The lodging sector is said to have moved past the post-pandemic boom into a more normalized operating environment where growth relies on network expansion and fee generation rather than rapid, post-lockdown price hikes.

Data center REIT Equinix led the decliners, retreating 3.91% to $985.98.

AI-related stocks and the tech sector plunged this week amid a growing concern among investors that the AI infrastructure boom could become increasingly difficult to finance, particularly if inflation keeps interest rates elevated and customers struggle to generate sufficient returns on their investments.

Prologis followed with a 2.89% pullback to $125.75. The stock got a boost with third-quarter earnings that exceeded analyst expectations. The REIT updated its 2026 core FFO per share guidance to a range of $6.25 to $6.29 from $6.22 to $6.30, against the Visible Alpha consensus of $6.27.

However, net earnings attributable to common stockholders per diluted share guidance was lowered to $4.05-$4.15 from $4.40-$4.55.

Alexandria Real Estate Equities topped the midcap losers. The stock price decreased 8.55% from the prior week to $41.62.

The data center REIT fell amid a broader tech fallout even after saying it signed a credit support agreement with AMD to support a lease for Phase 1 of its Project Matador energy and artificial intelligence facility in Texas covering 222 MW of gross power capacity, representing a key milestone toward securing project financing.

data.title: HDFC Bank reports muted 4.70% increase in Q2 standalone net profit at ₹19,510 cr
data.description:
HDFC Bank reported a muted 4.70 per cent year-on-year (y-o-y) increase in second quarter (Q2FY27) standalone net profit at ₹19,510 crore, with a decent rise in net interest income being offset by decline in other income and increase in tax expense.

India’s second largest bank, which logged a net profit of 18,641 crore in the year ago period, reported a robust growth in advances and improvement in asset quality in the reporting quarter.

Net interest income (interest income less interest expended) rose 10 per cent y-o-y to ₹34,619 crore (₹31,551.50 crore in Q2FY26).

Other income, comprising commission income from non-fund based banking activities, fees, earnings from forex and derivative transactions, profit and loss (including revaluation) from investments, dividends from subsidiaries and recoveries from accounts previously written off, declined 4 per cent y-o-y to ₹13,831 crore (₹14,350 crore). This is mainly due to treasury trading gains dipping significantly to ₹780 crore (₹2,390 crore).

Net interest margin declined to 3.16 per cent in the reporting quarter against 3.27 per cent in the year ago period.

Srinivasan Vaidyanathan, CFO, said: “There there were certain constraints and certain choices that we made over the last two quarters, and so the margin is slightly lower than where we had envisaged it would be. It would take a couple of more quarters to pull it back.”

Provisions nudged up 2 per cent y-o-y to ₹3,574 crore (₹3,501 crore). Tax expense rose 11 per cent y-o-y to ₹6,400 crore (₹5,782 crore).

NPA improves

Gross non-performing assets (NPAs) position improved to 1.11 per cent of gross advances as at September-end 2026 against 1.24 per cent as at September-end 2025. Net NPAs position too improved to 0.37 per cent of net advances against 0.42 per cent.

Total deposits grew by a robust 19 per cent y-o-y to stand at ₹33,27,449 crore as at September-end 2026. Low-cost current account, savings account (CASA) deposits declined to 31.6 per cent of total deposits as of September 30, 2026 from 33.9 per cent as of September 30, 2025.

data.title: SpaceX satellite system not fully operational in Ukraine yet, Zelensky says
data.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday that speed restrictions on SpaceX -owned Starlink and Starshield satellite networks remain in place despite earlier signs that the connectivity had been fully restored.

The Ukrainian military faced sudden speed restrictions on Starlink systems on Wednesday, prompting SpaceX CEO Elon Musk to suggest that the Trump administration was involved in the disruptions, a claim a senior U.S. official later denied.

While Kyiv confirmed that connectivity was restored by the next day, Zelensky says that speed restrictions at 161 kilometers per hour remain in place within Ukraine but not in neighboring countries of the European Union.

Citing a test conducted using vehicles equipped with Starlink devices, he said that the satellite systems, which continued to function in cars travelling at 180 kilometres per hour, disconnected once they crossed into Ukraine.

"The conclusion is that the restrictions apply inside Ukraine but do not apply in European Union countries. In other words, this is a planned operation," Zelensky said, adding that European partners are working on developing a possible alternative to Starlink.

SpaceX's satellite communications systems are vital for Ukraine's defensive capabilities, with Starlink-powered drones used to conduct reconnaissance missions and destroy Russian jet-powered drones.

data.title: Spain's hard left fails to unite before election, hurting chances of staying in power
data.description:
Key points:
  • Left-wing alliance talks collapse before deadline
  • Vote split could hurt Sanchez' re-election prospects
  • Candidate-list dispute drives rupture

By David Latona

Spain's hard-left parties on Saturday presented separate candidate lists for a snap election after talks on a nationwide pact collapsed, reducing Socialist prime minister Pedro Sanchez' chances of staying in power at the head of a leftist coalition.

Spain's electoral system disadvantages smaller parties running separately, particularly in less populous provinces, where fewer seats are available.

The division could also demoralise left-wing voters, whom organisers hoped to galvanise around housing protests and fear of the far right.

The Broad Front, a platform comprising several parties represented in the minority government, and the other main party on the hard left, Podemos ("We Can"), had been publicly arguing over the leading positions on joint candidate lists for the November 29 election in Madrid and Barcelona, the largest constituencies.

Long-standing animosities between former comrades-turned-rivals did not help.

"These past few days have been very difficult ... some people will be disappointed today, and for that I am sorry," Ada Colau, the former Barcelona mayor and leader of the Broad Front, said at her platform's launch event in Madrid.

Podemos, whose lead candidate is former equality minister Irene Montero, had proposed open primaries to determine candidates' positions on joint lists.

But the Broad Front refused, arguing there was too little time, and wanted its own preferred candidates to lead the lists in Madrid and Barcelona.

Podemos then made a separate pact deal with the Republican Left of Catalonia (ERC), which favours Catalan independence.

data.title: What investors need to know about America's fastest-growing coffee chain
data.description:
Drive-thru coffee chain 7 Brew is one of the most intriguing stories in the retail sector. The Arkansas-based company is growing rapidly and has a cult-like following thanks to its stripped-down menu, fast service, and energetic baristas. That recipe has put pressure on established coffee chains such as Starbucks , Dutch Bros , Dunkin', Scooter's Coffee, and Black Rock Coffee Bar , as well as convenience-store operators in some markets.

The chain grew from 24 stores at the start of 2023 to 604 at the start of 2026 and now has more than 800, having opened 62 stands across 26 states in August alone. It is on track to surpass 1,000 locations by year-end. Earlier this year, 7 Brew launched a mobile app, began selling canned coffee at Walmart , and announced its first college-campus stand.

Almost all the growth comes from franchisees rather than company-owned stores. The company's 2026 plan calls for 437 franchise openings and about 10 corporate openings, with large, well-funded franchise groups driving much of the expansion. Investors such as Blackstone are backing the growth. The business model centers on small, low-cost drive-thru or walk-up stands with no seating. These locations are primarily in suburban areas and smaller markets with limited coffee competition, and they serve sweet, highly customizable drinks.

For investors, Blackstone's backing has fueled speculation about a potential 7 Brew IPO. The list of companies that went public while Blackstone was an investor includes Pinnacle Foods , SeaWorld Entertainment , Catalent, and Invitation Homes .

data.title: Reliance Consumer Director, Blinkit officials among 10 booked in expired-food probe
data.description:
Police in Bhiwandi, Maharashtra’s Thane district, have registered an FIR against a Reliance Consumer Products director and nine others, including officials associated with Reliance Retail, Blinkit and Hyperpure, following a Food and Drug Administration (FDA) investigation into the alleged diversion of expired and rejected food products back into retail markets. The regulator seized stock worth ₹48.09 lakh during inspections across Thane and Pune districts on October 14–15 and suspended licences of five facilities linked to the companies, senior FDA officials told businessline.

The investigation centres on whether warehouse operators and disposal contractors failed to ensure that expired, damaged and customer-rejected food products were destroyed. Instead, the goods were allegedly diverted through unlicensed sorting yards, brokers and retailers before reaching consumers, the officials said.

The FIR, registered at Shanti Nagar police station, names V. Subramaniam, whole-time director of Reliance Consumer Products, alongside officials associated with Reliance Retail, Blinkit and Eternal’s business-to-business food-supplies arm Hyperpure. Others named include a disposal-agency operator, local suppliers and a discount-store owner. The case invokes provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act and Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

Five warehouse licences suspended

Seven FDA teams conducted coordinated inspections across Thane and Pune districts. Following hearings on October 15, the regulator suspended licences of Reliance Consumer Products and Reliance Retail facilities at Vadpe in Bhiwandi, a Reliance Retail warehouse at Chakan, Hyperpure’s Usatane facility and a Blinkit warehouse at Nighoje. The suspensions are facility-specific rather than company-wide.

The largest reported seizure, worth over ₹24 lakh, came from a Bhiwandi disposal yard. Officials also seized approximately ₹4.92 lakh of stock at Reliance Consumer Products’ Vadpe warehouse and ₹7.81 lakh at Hyperpure’s Usatane facility.

According to FDA officials, disposal agencies allegedly issued destruction certificates without adequately verifying that rejected goods had actually been destroyed. At unlicensed sorting yards, packets appearing saleable were separated and supplied to brokers and retailers. Expired and leaking products were subsequently found displayed for sale at an unlicensed Bhiwandi outlet.

Investigators also found alleged quantity mismatches and inconsistent consignor-consignee details in disposal records, raising questions about oversight of third-party contractors.

The case follows earlier FDA action against Amazon Retail India’s Bhiwandi warehouse over similar allegations. Its licence was suspended in June and subsequently cancelled. Amazon challenged the action in the Bombay High Court, which questioned the regulator’s approach and later ordered an interim arrangement for scientific disposal of expired stock.

Investigators must now establish whether warehouse operators verified actual destruction of rejected stock and determine responsibility across the disposal chain. The allegations remain under investigation.

data.title: DLF acquires 7.5 acres in Gurugram to expand luxury housing project
data.description:
DLF Ltd has acquired a 7.5-acre land in Gurugram to build a housing project as part of its expansion plan amid strong demand for luxury homes.

This plot is contiguous to 28 acres on Golf Course Extension Road that the company acquired in early 2024 from IREO, after taking over bad loans worth Rs 825 crore related to the land.

“We entered into a collaboration for a fresh 7.48 acres of land, which is contiguous to the 28 acres. So, eventually, it will be a 36-acre land parcel contiguous in Sector 61 (Gurugram) that we will have,” Managing Director Ashok Tyagi told analysts in a conference call on Saturday.

He said the company has made small payments to lenders in the September quarter towards this additional land parcel.

According to an investor presentation, DLF invested Rs 353 crore in the September quarter on payments related to land acquisition. In the first quarter of this fiscal, it had spent Rs 210 crore.

Tyagi said the land deal is expected to be completed by March end, but did not disclose the total land cost.

He also did not tell the timeline for launch of the housing project on this contiguous 36-acre plot.

Earlier acquisition involved ₹825-crore loan

According to a regulatory filing in 2024, DLF had entered into an agreement with Standard Chartered Bank, Singapore Branch, DB International (Asia), Singapore and Deutsche Investments India (lender/bond holder).

From these lenders, DLF agreed to buy non-convertible, redeemable bonds issued by IREO (bond issuer).

“Rs 825 crore was the outstanding loan that the developer had with these two banks. Actually, the loan was about Rs 1,200 crore. The bankers agreed to take a hair cut as a one-time settlement. So, Rs 825 crore is what we have bought the loan at from the bankers,” Tyagi had said in 2024.

Development potential to increase

The total development potential for the initial 28-acre plot is 7.5 million square ft, which will now increase significantly.

The Golf Course Extension Road has become an important micro market in the Gurugram residential market, with many leading developers launching luxury projects in this area.

DLF’s real estate portfolio

India’s largest realty firm DLF Ltd has developed more than 185 real estate projects so far, covering more than 352 million square feet of area.

The group has 275 million sq ft of development potential across residential and commercial segments, including current projects under execution.

data.title: ICICI Bank Q2 profit jumps 20.1% to ₹14,843 crore; margins come under pressure
data.description:
ICICI Bank reported a 20.1 per cent year-on-year increase in net profit to ₹14,843 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, driven by strong growth in net interest income (NII). The bank posted a profit after tax (PAT) of ₹12,359 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year. However, PAT remained largely flat sequentially.

Net interest income rises 17.7 per cent

The bank’s net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned and interest paid, rose 17.7 per cent to ₹R25,338.7 crore during the reporting quarter, compared with ₹21,529.5 crore a year earlier. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, NII increased 3.9 per cent to ₹24,384.4 crore.

Loan book expands 30 per cent

ICICI Bank’s loan book expanded 30 per cent year-on-year to ₹18.3 lakh crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with ₹14.08 lakh crore in the same period last year. Advances grew 12 per cent sequentially. Excluding the leverage provided on FCNR(B) loans, the bank’s lending grew 24.1 per cent year-on-year and 7.3 per cent quarter-on-quarter.

Deposits grow on FCNR(B) inflows

Deposits rose 27.1 per cent to ₹2.04 lakh crore in the quarter under review, up from ₹1.6 lakh crore in the year-ago period. Sequentially, deposits rose 11.8 per cent to ₹1.8 lakh crore from ₹ 1.6 lakh crore in the previous quarter.

FCNR(B) inflows contributed significantly to deposit growth. Excluding these NRI inflows, total deposits grew 17 per cent year-on-year and 3.1 per cent quarter-on-quarter as of September 30, 2026.

Net interest margin contracts

Despite strong profitability and business growth, the bank’s margins came under pressure. Net interest margin (NIM) fell to 4.18 per cent in the reporting quarter, down from 4.30 per cent in the year-ago period, a contraction of 12 basis points. The Q2 NIM was also 18 basis points lower than the 4.36 per cent recorded in the previous quarter. Excluding the benefit of interest income from a tax refund, the bank’s NIM stood at 4.28 per cent in the preceding quarter. On this adjusted basis, NIM fell by about 10 basis points in Q2.

Addressing the margin contraction, ICICI Bank Executive Director Sandeep Batra said the decline was largely attributable to the cost of FCNR(B) inflows. “Talking of the decline from 4.28 per cent to 4.18 per cent, it is largely a function of FCNR(B), which results in a higher deposit base and a lower CASA ratio,” Batra said during the media call.

data.title: Axis Bank Q2 profit rises 37.6% to ₹7,003 crore as provisions fall 52.2%
data.description:
Axis Bank reported a 37.6 per cent year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to ₹7,003 crore for the quarter ended September 2026, driven by strong core income growth, robust loan book expansion, and a sharp decline in provisioning costs. The lender had posted a net profit of ₹5,090 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Sequentially, profit eased marginally by 1.6 per cent to ₹7,114 crore from ₹7,214 crore in Q1 FY27.

Net interest income rises 12 per cent

The bank’s net interest income (NII) grew 12 per cent year-on-year to ₹15,371 crore from ₹13,745 crore in Q2 FY26. Sequentially, NII grew around 5 per cent, supported by strong momentum across retail, SME and wholesale banking businesses. Net interest margin (NIM) stood at 3.36 per cent during the quarter and 3.47 per cent excluding the impact of FCNR(B) deposits, reflecting margin resilience amid a competitive funding environment.

Advances grow across retail, SME and wholesale businesses

The strong earnings growth was underpinned by healthy loan growth across businesses. Total advances grew 23 per cent year-on-year and 9 per cent quarter-on-quarter, while advances excluding loans linked to FCNR(B) deposits increased 19 per cent year-on-year. Retail advances expanded 16 per cent year-on-year, driven by healthy disbursement trends across products. The SME portfolio continued to outperform, growing 25 per cent year-on-year, supported by differentiated offerings and technology-led capabilities, while the wholesale banking franchise grew 34 per cent year-on-year on robust client activity and deeper relationship-led engagement.

Lower provisions boost profitability

Operating profit stood at ₹11,083 crore, up 6.4 per cent year-on-year but down 4.9 per cent sequentially from ₹11,659 crore in the June quarter, as operating expenses rose faster than revenue. Operating expenses increased to ₹10,819 crore from ₹9,722 crore in the preceding quarter, led by higher employee expenses and other operating costs. Employee costs rose to ₹3,314 crore from ₹3,058 crore. Lower provisioning drove profit growth during the quarter. Provisions and contingencies fell 52.2 per cent year-on-year to ₹1,694 crore from ₹3,547 crore, helping profit before tax rise 36.8 per cent to ₹9,389 crore.

Management highlights growth and risk discipline

“Growth was achieved through higher wallet share from existing customers while maintaining disciplined risk thresholds,” said Amitabh Chaudhry, MD & CEO of Axis Bank. “We delivered robust growth in deposits and advances, supported by strong NII growth, improving asset quality and healthy operating performance, while maintaining strong liquidity and capital buffers to support future growth,” said Rajeev Mantri, Group CFO, Axis Bank.

Deposits grow as asset quality improves

On the liability side, total deposits grew 23 per cent year-on-year, supported by strong growth in term deposits, CASA balances, and FCNR(B) inflows. Asset quality remained a key positive, with the gross NPA ratio improving to 1.16 per cent from 1.46 per cent a year ago and the net NPA ratio declining to 0.35 per cent from 0.44 per cent. Net credit cost reduced to 0.45 per cent, reflecting lower stress formation and prudent risk management. Improved asset quality, along with strong operating performance, was a major contributor to the sharp rise in profits during the quarter.

Rahul Shukla appointed Group Head

Separately, the bank appointed Rahul Shukla as Group Head, Commercial and Bharat Banking, effective October 19, 2026, strengthening its senior management team.

data.title: HDFC Bank veteran Kaizad Bharucha quits
data.description:
In a major shake-up at HDFC Bank, its Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha has decided to quit, after being passed over for appointment as Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer  of India’s largest private sector bank.

This comes about a fortnight after RBI approved the Bank’s application for appointment of Anup Bagchi (former Chief of ICICI Life Insurance, who joined HDFC Bank’s board as an Additional Director with effect from October 2, 2026) as its MD & CEO for three years with effect from October 27, 2026.

Bharucha is HDFC Bank’s longest serving board member, having joined it in 2014. He was re-appointed Whole-time Director/WTD (Deputy Managing Director) of the Bank for three years with effect from April 19, 2026.

Late August 2026, Sashidhar Jagdishan decided not to seek re-appointment as the MD&CEO  of HDFC Bank for a third term amid controversy that started with the abrupt resignation of the Bank’s Part-Time Chairman in March 2026. His term ends on October 26, 2026.

The Bank on Saturday informed the exchanges that Bharucha has requested cessation from the service of the Bank with effect from the close of business hours on December 31, 2026.

“The GNRC (Governance, Nomination and Remuneration Committee) and the Board of Directors, at their respective meetings held on October 16, 2026 and October 17, 2026, respected the decision of Bharucha and accepted his request to be forwarded to the RBI for approval,” per the Bank’s filing.

With two veterans — Sashidhar and Bharucha -moving on, HDFC Bank will have two new WTDs — Bagchi and a new candidate, who could either be an insider or an outsider.

In September 2026, the Bank sought RBI’s approval for appointment of Jimmy Tata (currently Chief Credit Offocer) as a WTD designated as Executive Director) of the Bank for three years.

In a media concall, Jagdishan emphasised that HDFC Bank has been driven more by processes and not by an individual personality. Further, the depth in management is so large that the continuity and the ethos of the institution will be intact as well.

‘So Anup comes in and he will lead a team of able leaders who have been with the institution for a long time…and they will be the fulcrum (of the organisation) and ably support Anup to chart out his vision and his strategy as well. So, you know, he has about 34 years of experience in the field of financial services,” said Jagdishan, adding that “ he is a seasoned player who has been not just in banking, but also in insurance. So he has a very holistic view….So I wish him the very best, and you will hear more from him going forward.”

Bagchi, who joined the call, said: “I’m going to engage with all — the regulators, customers, stakeholders, and gather insights, and that will become a key input to our operational priorities.  And if you look at the leadership, they have spent many, many years within this system. And they know the system, they are fully committed to the institution. So, in fact, I’m very, very lucky to be a part of an institution which is solid, very sound.”

data.title: FSSAI issues notices to Nestle, HUL for misleading claims
data.description:
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India on Saturday said that it has issued notices to Nestlé India and Hindustan Unilever regarding misleading claims and non-compliances with regards to certain products. It has also suspended licences of Sukhdarshan Pharma and Bala Ji Food Products for serious food safety violations. This comes as recent inspections and audits have led to strict enforcement actions against several major brand manufacturers and local FBOs for misleading claims, non-compliance with labelling regulations, and severe food safety violations.

The food safety regulator said that Nestle India was found marketing and selling “Nescafé Intense Café” Cappuccino flavour, “Nescafé Choco Mocha” and “Nescafé Chilled Latte” on e-commerce platforms with “inconsistent descriptions on the packaging.”

The products, manufactured by Schreiber Dynamix Dairies and Lotus Dairy Products were found to be making the declaration of “Flavoured Milk” in the front of the pack while the back of the pack declares, ““Proprietary Food – 1.12 Dairy Based Drink.”

It added that the e-commerce listings also described the products as “Coffee Flavoured Milk”,resulting in inconsistency between the product label and its advertisements. “

It also noted that the product descriptions on e-commerce platforms were found to contain claims such as “crafted with the goodness of flavoured double toned milk”, which are not consistent with the declared composition and category of the product. It added that since the products fall under the category of “Flavoured Milks”, the company’s declaration as proprietary food was found to be “incorrect.” “Such inconsistent labelling, product descriptions and advertisements were found to be in contravention of the applicable provision of the FSS (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018 and FSS (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2020,” it said.

Misleading claims

In a separate notice issued to Nestle India, the FSSAI has flagged misleading claims on the company’s “renal resource vanilla flavour powder.” It said that the examination of the product label, ad and product listing on the e-commerce platform revealed non-compliances. It noted that the product is intended for a special medical condition and requires prior approval of the FSSAI, which has not been obtained by the company rendering it non-compliant.

The food safety regulator has also issued two notices to Hindustan Unilever for Horlicks Women’s Plus Chocolate Nutrition Drink and Horlicks Mother’s Plus Kesar for misleading claims. FSSAI has flagged claims such as “nutrition for strong bones” and “clinically proven to help improve bone strength” as “misleading or non-compliant” with regulations.

It noted that use of the term “healthy” in food claims found to be on Horlicks’ Women Plus is in contravention with the regulations. Nutritional Information was also not provided in the prescribed form. Also the claim of “100 per cent RDA of Calcium, Vitamin D & K2” was found not to comply with food safety requirements. In the case of Horlicks Mother’s Plus Kesar, FSSAI has flagged claims such as “Healthy Birth Weight” on the product label and “For baby’s healthy birth weight” in the advertisement as potentially misleading and in contravention of the FSS (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018.

The food safety regulator also said it has suspended the licence of Sukhdarshan Pharma for serious food safety, hygiene and sanitation violations. Meanwhile, the regulator has also suspended the license of Bala Ji Food Products due to serious food safety violation and continued non-compliance with applicable food safety requirements.
